38	    coordinate_system = x_coord.coord_system

42	        projection = coordinate_system.as_cartopy_projection()
43	        x_grid, y_grid = np.meshgrid(x_coord.points, y_coord.points)
44	        geographic = ccrs.PlateCarree()
45	        locations = geographic.transform_points(projection, x_grid, y_grid)
46	        longitude = locations[..., 0]
47	        latitude = locations[..., 1]
48	
49	        station_rows: list[tuple[float, float, float]] = []

34	recorded in the original implementation.

37	actions.  This mimics older behaviour, so is still useful while we are still

88	    # Wrap an action function with some standard behaviour.
89	    # Notably : engages with the rules logging process.
90	    @wraps(func)
91	    def inner(engine, *args, **kwargs):
92	        # Call the original rules-func
93	        rule_name = func(engine, *args, **kwargs)
94	        if rule_name is None:
95	            # Work out the corresponding rule name, and log it.
96	            # Note: an action returns a name string, which identifies it,
97	            # but also may vary depending on whether it successfully
98	            # triggered, and if so what it matched.
99	            rule_name = _default_rulenamesfunc(func.__name__)
100	        engine.rules_triggered.add(rule_name)
101	
102	    func._rulenames_func = _default_rulenamesfunc

285	def action_build_dimension_coordinate(engine, providescoord_fact):
286	    """Convert a CFCoordinateVariable into a cube dim-coord."""
287	    coord_type, var_name = providescoord_fact
288	    cf_var = engine.cf_var.cf_group[var_name]
289	    rule_name = f"fc_build_coordinate_({coord_type})"
290	    coord_grid_class, coord_name = _COORDTYPE_GRIDTYPES_AND_COORDNAMES[
291	        coord_type
292	    ]
293	    if coord_grid_class is None:
294	        # Coordinates not identified with a specific grid-type class (latlon,
295	        # rotated or projected) are always built, but can have no coord-system.
296	        coord_system = None  # no coord-system can be used
297	        succeed = True
298	    else:
299	        grid_classes = ("latlon", "rotated", "projected")
300	        assert coord_grid_class in grid_classes
301	        # If a coord is of a type identified with a grid, we may have a
302	        # coordinate system (i.e. a valid grid-mapping).
303	        # N.B. this requires each grid-type identification to validate the
304	        # coord var (e.g. "is_longitude").
305	        # Non-conforming lon/lat/projection coords will be classed as
306	        # dim-coords by cf.py, but 'action_provides_coordinate' will give them
307	        # a coord-type of 'miscellaneous' : hence, they have no coord-system.
308	        coord_system = engine.cube_parts.get("coordinate_system")
309	        # Translate the specific grid-mapping type to a grid-class
310	        if coord_system is None:
311	            succeed = True
312	            cs_gridclass = None
313	        else:
314	            # Get a grid-class from the grid-type
315	            # i.e. one of latlon/rotated/projected, as for coord_grid_class.
316	            gridtypes_factlist = engine.fact_list("grid-type")
317	            (gridtypes_fact,) = gridtypes_factlist  # only 1 fact
318	            (cs_gridtype,) = gridtypes_fact  # fact contains 1 term
319	            if cs_gridtype == "latitude_longitude":
320	                cs_gridclass = "latlon"
321	            elif cs_gridtype == "rotated_latitude_longitude":
322	                cs_gridclass = "rotated"
323	            else:
324	                # Other specific projections
325	                assert cs_gridtype is not None
326	                cs_gridclass = "projected"
327	
328	        assert cs_gridclass in grid_classes + (None,)
329	
330	        if coord_grid_class == "latlon":
331	            if cs_gridclass == "latlon":
332	                succeed = True
333	            elif cs_gridclass is None:
334	                succeed = True
335	                rule_name += "(no-cs)"
336	            elif cs_gridclass == "rotated":
337	                # We disallow this case
338	                succeed = False
339	                rule_name += "(FAILED : latlon coord with rotated cs)"
340	            else:
341	                assert cs_gridclass == "projected"
342	                # succeed, no error, but discards the coord-system
343	                # TODO: could issue a warning in this case ?
344	                succeed = True
345	                coord_system = None
346	                rule_name += "(no-cs : discarded projected cs)"
347	        elif coord_grid_class == "rotated":
348	            if cs_gridclass == "rotated":
349	                succeed = True
350	                rule_name += "(rotated)"
351	            elif cs_gridclass is None:
352	                succeed = True
353	                rule_name += "(rotated no-cs)"
354	            elif cs_gridclass == "latlon":
355	                # We disallow this case
356	                succeed = False
357	                rule_name += "(FAILED rotated coord with latlon cs)"
358	            else:
359	                assert cs_gridclass == "projected"
360	                succeed = True
361	                coord_system = None
362	                rule_name += "(rotated no-cs : discarded projected cs)"
363	        elif coord_grid_class == "projected":
364	            # In this case, can *only* build a coord at all if there is a
365	            # coord-system of the correct class (i.e. 'projected').
366	            succeed = cs_gridclass == "projected"
367	            if not succeed:
368	                rule_name += "(FAILED projected coord with non-projected cs)"
369	        else:
370	            # Just FYI : literally not possible, as we already asserted this.
371	            assert coord_grid_class in grid_classes
372	
373	    if succeed:
374	        hh.build_dimension_coordinate(
375	            engine, cf_var, coord_name=coord_name, coord_system=coord_system
376	        )
377	    return rule_name

542	def run_actions(engine):
543	    """
544	    Run all actions for a cube.
545	
546	    This is the top-level "activation" function which runs all the appropriate
547	    rules actions to translate facts and build all the cube elements.
548	
549	    The specific cube being translated is "engine.cube".
550	
551	    """
552	
553	    # default (all cubes) action, always runs
554	    action_default(engine)  # This should run the default rules.
555	
556	    # deal with grid-mappings
557	    grid_mapping_facts = engine.fact_list("grid_mapping")
558	    # For now, there should be at most *one* of these.
559	    assert len(grid_mapping_facts) in (0, 1)
560	    for grid_mapping_fact in grid_mapping_facts:
561	        action_provides_grid_mapping(engine, grid_mapping_fact)
562	
563	    # identify + record aka "PROVIDE" specific named coordinates
564	    # N.B. cf.py has identified that these are dim-coords, NOT aux-coords
565	    # (which are recorded separately).
566	    # TODO: can probably remove this step ??
567	    dimcoord_facts = engine.fact_list("coordinate")
568	    for dimcoord_fact in dimcoord_facts:
569	        action_provides_coordinate(engine, dimcoord_fact)
570	
571	    # build (dimension) coordinates
572	    # The 'provides' step and the grid-mapping must have already been done.
573	    providescoord_facts = engine.fact_list("provides-coordinate-(oftype)")
574	    for providescoord_fact in providescoord_facts:
575	        action_build_dimension_coordinate(engine, providescoord_fact)
576	
577	    # build aux-coords
578	    auxcoord_facts = engine.fact_list("auxiliary_coordinate")
579	    for auxcoord_fact in auxcoord_facts:
580	        action_build_auxiliary_coordinate(engine, auxcoord_fact)
581	
582	    # Detect + process and special 'ukmo' attributes
583	    # Run on every cube : they choose themselves whether to trigger.
584	    action_ukmo_stash(engine)
585	    action_ukmo_processflags(engine)
586	
587	    # cell measures
588	    cellm_facts = engine.fact_list("cell_measure")
589	    for cellm_fact in cellm_facts:
590	        action_build_cell_measure(engine, cellm_fact)
591	
592	    # ancillary variables

260	def _split_cell_methods(nc_cell_methods: str) -> List[re.Match]:
261	    """
262	    Split a CF cell_methods attribute string into a list of zero or more cell
263	    methods, each of which is then parsed with a regex to return a list of match
264	    objects.
265	
266	    Args:
267	
268	    * nc_cell_methods: The value of the cell methods attribute to be split.
269	
270	    Returns:
271	
272	    * nc_cell_methods_matches: A list of the re.Match objects associated with
273	      each parsed cell method
274	
275	    Splitting is done based on words followed by colons outside of any brackets.
276	    Validation of anything other than being laid out in the expected format is
277	    left to the calling function.
278	    """
279	
280	    # Find name candidates
281	    name_start_inds = []
282	    for m in _CM_PARSE_NAME.finditer(nc_cell_methods):
283	        name_start_inds.append(m.start())
284	
285	    # Remove those that fall inside brackets
286	    bracket_depth = 0
287	    for ind, cha in enumerate(nc_cell_methods):
288	        if cha == "(":
289	            bracket_depth += 1
290	        elif cha == ")":
291	            bracket_depth -= 1
292	            if bracket_depth < 0:
293	                msg = (
294	                    "Cell methods may be incorrectly parsed due to mismatched "
295	                    "brackets"
296	                )
297	                warnings.warn(
298	                    msg,
299	                    category=iris.exceptions.IrisCfLoadWarning,
300	                    stacklevel=2,
301	                )
302	        if bracket_depth > 0 and ind in name_start_inds:
303	            name_start_inds.remove(ind)
304	
305	    # List tuples of indices of starts and ends of the cell methods in the string
306	    method_indices = []
307	    for ii in range(len(name_start_inds) - 1):
308	        method_indices.append((name_start_inds[ii], name_start_inds[ii + 1]))
309	    method_indices.append((name_start_inds[-1], len(nc_cell_methods)))
310	
311	    # Index the string and match against each substring
312	    nc_cell_methods_matches = []
313	    for start_ind, end_ind in method_indices:
314	        nc_cell_method_str = nc_cell_methods[start_ind:end_ind]
315	        nc_cell_method_match = _CM_PARSE.match(nc_cell_method_str.strip())
316	        if not nc_cell_method_match:
317	            msg = (
318	                f"Failed to fully parse cell method string: {nc_cell_methods}"
319	            )
320	            warnings.warn(
321	                msg, category=iris.exceptions.IrisCfLoadWarning, stacklevel=2
322	            )
323	            continue
324	        nc_cell_methods_matches.append(nc_cell_method_match)
325	
326	    return nc_cell_methods_matches

338	def parse_cell_methods(nc_cell_methods):
339	    """
340	    Parse a CF cell_methods attribute string into a tuple of zero or
341	    more CellMethod instances.
342	
343	    Args:
344	
345	    * nc_cell_methods (str):
346	        The value of the cell methods attribute to be parsed.
347	
348	    Returns:
349	
350	    * cell_methods
351	        An iterable of :class:`iris.coords.CellMethod`.
352	
353	    Multiple coordinates, intervals and comments are supported.
354	    If a method has a non-standard name a warning will be issued, but the
355	    results are not affected.
356	
357	    """
358	
359	    cell_methods = []
360	    if nc_cell_methods is not None:
361	        for m in _split_cell_methods(nc_cell_methods):
362	            d = m.groupdict()
363	            method = d[_CM_METHOD]
364	            method = method.strip()
365	            # Check validity of method, allowing for multi-part methods
366	            # e.g. mean over years.
367	            method_words = method.split()
368	            if method_words[0].lower() not in _CM_KNOWN_METHODS:
369	                msg = "NetCDF variable contains unknown cell method {!r}"
370	                warnings.warn(
371	                    msg.format("{}".format(method_words[0])),
372	                    category=UnknownCellMethodWarning,
373	                )
374	            d[_CM_METHOD] = method
375	            name = d[_CM_NAME]
376	            name = name.replace(" ", "")
377	            name = name.rstrip(":")
378	            d[_CM_NAME] = tuple([n for n in name.split(":")])
379	            interval = []
380	            comment = []
381	            if d[_CM_EXTRA] is not None:
382	                #
383	                # tokenise the key words and field colon marker
384	                #
385	                d[_CM_EXTRA] = d[_CM_EXTRA].replace(
386	                    "comment:", "<<comment>><<:>>"
387	                )
388	                d[_CM_EXTRA] = d[_CM_EXTRA].replace(
389	                    "interval:", "<<interval>><<:>>"
390	                )
391	                d[_CM_EXTRA] = d[_CM_EXTRA].split("<<:>>")
392	                if len(d[_CM_EXTRA]) == 1:
393	                    comment.extend(d[_CM_EXTRA])
394	                else:
395	                    next_field_type = comment
396	                    for field in d[_CM_EXTRA]:
397	                        field_type = next_field_type
398	                        index = field.rfind("<<interval>>")
399	                        if index == 0:
400	                            next_field_type = interval
401	                            continue
402	                        elif index > 0:
403	                            next_field_type = interval
404	                        else:
405	                            index = field.rfind("<<comment>>")
406	                            if index == 0:
407	                                next_field_type = comment
408	                                continue
409	                            elif index > 0:
410	                                next_field_type = comment
411	                        if index != -1:
412	                            field = field[:index]
413	                        field_type.append(field.strip())
414	            #
415	            # cater for a shared interval over multiple axes
416	            #
417	            if len(interval):
418	                if len(d[_CM_NAME]) != len(interval) and len(interval) == 1:
419	                    interval = interval * len(d[_CM_NAME])
420	            #
421	            # cater for a shared comment over multiple axes
422	            #
423	            if len(comment):
424	                if len(d[_CM_NAME]) != len(comment) and len(comment) == 1:
425	                    comment = comment * len(d[_CM_NAME])
426	            d[_CM_INTERVAL] = tuple(interval)
427	            d[_CM_COMMENT] = tuple(comment)
428	            cell_method = iris.coords.CellMethod(
429	                d[_CM_METHOD],
430	                coords=d[_CM_NAME],
431	                intervals=d[_CM_INTERVAL],
432	                comments=d[_CM_COMMENT],
433	            )
434	            cell_methods.append(cell_method)

        #: The azimuth of the central line, degrees clockwise from north at
